subject: Calmer
fact: Calmer is the cleric of St. Cuthbert who burned with righteous fury at the gnoll, killed it with hatred for demonic beings, and later insisted on precautions in Nulb, barricading a door and positioning Zephyr to watch the window while muttering about exhaustion from dealing with evil powers.

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr attempted to politely question the gnoll, slapped it to demand information, was positioned by Calmer to watch the window in Nulb, and descended with the party into the pit beneath the Temple of Elemental Evil.

subject: Dick Rentsch
fact: Dick Rentsch is the contact in Nulb who arranged a meeting with Romag, led the party into the Temple of Elemental Evil through a side entrance, described the temple as his happy place, explained its future role in the Earth Temple’s purge, led them down into the pit, opened a secret door with a knock pattern, and warned them not to disturb the bones in the corridor.

subject: Romag
fact: Romag is a powerful figure within the Temple of Elemental Evil whom Dick Rentsch arranged to meet, though the party has not yet encountered them directly.

subject: Temple of Elemental Evil
fact: The Temple of Elemental Evil is a massive, leprous gray monument to darkness with ruined architecture, obscene carvings, and a pervasive aura of vileness; it is currently empty but intended to be filled with supplicants who will kill and bury alive opponents after the Earth Temple destroys false prophets.

subject: Earth Temple
fact: The Earth Temple is a rival faction that plans to destroy false prophets and fill the Temple of Elemental Evil with devoted supplicants who will slaughter all who oppose them.

subject: Circle of Eight
fact: The Circle of Eight, including Mordenkainen and Bigby, once came to the Temple of Elemental Evil and performed mighty magic to seal it, as recalled by the party from Spugnoir’s story in Hommlet.

subject: Nulb
fact: Nulb is a town where the party met Dick Rentsch at the Waterside Hostel, received instructions to proceed to the Temple of Elemental Evil, and took precautions before departure, including barricading a door and watching windows.

subject: Temple of Elemental Evil
fact: The Temple of Elemental Evil is a vast, ruined structure with a northeast tower, obscene arched buttresses, carved leering faces, and a pervasive sense of fear; its main entrance has twenty-three-foot-high bronze doors sealed with iron chains and glowing runes, while a side entrance leads into a vestibule with horrifying murals, pinkish mineral pillars, and a central altar with a bloodstained human-shaped depression and a circular pit below.

subject: Pit beneath the Temple of Elemental Evil
fact: The pit is a twenty-foot-diameter circular shaft surrounded by broken crystal vessels, with a narrow spiral ledge descending its northern face to steep steps below, where a secret door opens into a bone-covered corridor after a specific knock pattern.

subject: Bone Corridor
fact: The Bone Corridor is at least one hundred feet long and twenty feet wide, entirely covered in a jumble of human and humanoid skeletons, many wearing sundered armor or clutching broken weapons, and inhabited by animated gnoll skeletons that rose to attack the party as they passed.

subject: Scroll with ancient markings
fact: A scroll bearing ancient markings was discovered on the bodies of the dead, though its contents and origin remain unexamined.

subject: Three ornate gold buttons
fact: Three ornate gold buttons were found on the bodies, marked as symbols of service to the Temple of Fire.

subject: Glowing runes on bronze doors
fact: Glowing runes burned with silvery radiance upon the twenty-three-foot-high bronze doors of the Temple of Elemental Evil, causing the party’s eyes to water when looked upon, and were deliberately avoided by Dick Rentsch.

subject: Central altar of pinkish-white marble
fact: The central altar is carved with a disturbing human-shaped depression stained dark with old blood, located in a chamber beneath the temple’s vestibule, and surrounded by a circular pit.

subject: Broken crystal vessels
fact: Shards of broken crystal vessels surround the circular pit beneath the central altar, their purpose and origin unknown.

subject: Animated gnoll skeletons
fact: Several gnoll skeletons suddenly animated and rose from the bone pile in the corridor to attack the party as they followed Dick Rentsch eastward.

subject: Gnoll
fact: A captured gnoll, bound and snarling, was interrogated by Zephyr and killed by Calmer with righteous fury, identified as a spawn of demon powers born from hyenas.

subject: Sealing of the Temple of Elemental Evil
fact: The Circle of Eight performed mighty magic to seal the Temple of Elemental Evil, as recalled by the party from Spugnoir’s tale in Hommlet.

subject: Opening of the secret door
fact: Dick Rentsch knocked on a wall in a specific pattern, triggering the opening of a secret door that revealed the Bone Corridor.

subject: Descent into the pit
fact: The party descended into the twenty-foot-diameter pit using a spiral ledge and steep steps, after Calmer requested rope for safety and Dick Rentsch reluctantly allowed them to tie themselves together.

subject: Fate of the Temple of Fire symbols
fact: Symbols marking the dead as servants of the Temple of Fire were found on the bodies, but their connection to the current Temple of Elemental Evil remains unexplained.

subject: Identity of the mysterious fungus
fact: Strange fungus, unlike any seen before, covered bones and vegetation in the temple grounds and pit, but its origin and properties are unknown.

subject: Purpose of the human-shaped depression
fact: The human-shaped depression on the central altar is stained with old blood; its ritual or functional purpose remains unexplained.

subject: Nature of Dick Rentsch’s allegiance
fact: Dick Rentsch is disturbingly at ease in the Temple of Elemental Evil and calls it his happy place; his true allegiance and role within the temple are unclear.

subject: Origin of the great battle in the Bone Corridor
fact: The Bone Corridor is filled with skeletons from a great battle, but the identity of the combatants and the cause of the conflict remain unknown.

subject: Romag
fact: Romag is the High Priest of the Earth Temple, who welcomed the party, requested the Chest of Rao, and revealed that the Earth Temple’s true power lies in the deeper levels beneath the elemental temples, all locked in conflict. His mission is for them to destroy the other temples so the Earth Temple may seize ultimate power.
source_quote: Romag laughed heartily at their ignorance, explaining that the surface temple was merely the beginning, and that the true power lay in the deeper levels descending into the very pit of evil itself.

subject: Dick Rentsch
fact: Dick Rentsch is the party’s liaison who brought them to Romag, provided them with a map of gnoll territories, and failed to disclose that they were being sent into enemy elemental territory. His actions suggest either incompetence or deliberate deception.
source_quote: Dick Rentsch provided them with a map showing where the gnolls could be found, explaining that they would need to navigate through territory controlled by multiple hostile factions.

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr is a party member who engaged in combat with undead and wraiths, suffered life-draining wounds from the wraith that reduced their maximum vitality, and was the target of lighthearted banter about their tiefling horns.
source_quote: The wraith’s spectral touch drained Zephyr’s very life essence, not only wounding him but reducing his maximum vitality in a way that could only be restored through extended rest or powerful healing magic.

subject: Calmer
fact: Calmer is a party member who repeatedly calls upon the power of St. Cuthbert to damage undead, including destroying skeletons and repelling the wraith. He is the first to voice suspicion about Dick Rentsch’s omissions.
source_quote: Calmer moved away, stating grimly that he was beginning to think Dick hadn’t told them everything about what awaited them here.

subject: Earth Temple
fact: The Earth Temple is one of four elemental temples locked in constant conflict with Fire, Water, and Air temples. It seeks ultimate dominance by destroying the others, operates from deep subterranean levels, and grants the badge of Earth to those who prove their loyalty and capability.
source_quote: Romag’s mission for them was clear: destroy the other temples so the Earth Temple could seize ultimate power. Romag promised that once they proved themselves capable of operating within the temple by completing this mission, they would earn the right to wear the badge of Earth.

subject: Fire Temple
fact: The Fire Temple is a rival elemental faction, hated by the Earth Temple. Its head, Alremm, is targeted for destruction by Earth Temple guards, and its influence extends into the deeper levels of the Temple of Elemental Evil.
source_quote: The guards expressed their loyalty to the Earth Temple and their hatred for the Fire Temple, boasting that once they killed enough gnolls, Alremm—the head of the Fire Temple—would be theirs.

subject: Air Temple
fact: The Air Temple is a rival elemental faction whose power source is located in the octagonal chamber below the dungeon floor, marked by glowing mist, a bronze square, and crystal braziers. The party has inadvertently entered this enemy territory, unaware until confronted by the wraith.
source_quote: The party regrouped, realizing with growing concern that they were standing in what was clearly the Air Temple’s power source.

subject: arrival at Air Temple power source
fact: The party descended into a hidden octagonal chamber fifteen feet below the dungeon floor, illuminated by milky radiance and filled with glowing mist, where they encountered a wraith—confirming they had entered the Air Temple’s sacred and hostile power core.
source_quote: They arrived in a large octagonal room fifteen feet below the normal dungeon floor, illuminated by an eerie milky radiance emanating from the ceiling, walls, and floor.

subject: wraith
fact: A wraith manifested in the Air Temple’s power chamber, attacking the party with life-draining spectral touch that reduces maximum vitality. It was repelled by Calmer’s divine power but remains a lethal threat capable of extended recovery.
source_quote: Immediately a wraith materialized before them—a terrifying undead spirit of malevolent power. Its spectral touch drained Zephyr’s very life essence, not only wounding him but reducing his maximum vitality in a way that could only be restored through extended rest or powerful healing magic.

subject: Chest of Rao
fact: The Chest of Rao is a sacred artifact presented to Romag by the party, confirming their compliance with his initial demand and serving as proof of their usefulness to the Earth Temple.
source_quote: He asked for the Chest of Rao, and the party presented it to him.

subject: map of gnoll territories
fact: Dick Rentsch provided the party with a map showing gnoll locations and hostile faction-controlled territory, but omitted that the path led directly into the Air Temple’s domain.
source_quote: Dick Rentsch provided them with a map showing where the gnolls could be found, explaining that they would need to navigate through territory controlled by multiple hostile factions.

subject: alabaster block with two knives and a crystal bowl
fact: An alabaster block bearing two knives and a crystal bowl is positioned south of the pit in the Air Temple’s chamber, likely a ritual or symbolic artifact tied to its elemental power.
source_quote: South of the pit sat an alabaster block bearing two knives and a crystal bowl, while crystal braziers suspended from silver chains emitted sickly sweet perfume smoke.

subject: Temple of Elemental Evil
fact: The Temple of Elemental Evil is a vast, multi-level subterranean complex divided among the Earth, Fire, Water, and Air temples, all locked in conflict. The deeper levels contain ancient evil, hidden secrets, and power sources guarded by undead and hostile factions.
source_quote: They were now deep within the Temple of Elemental Evil, surrounded by ancient evil and warring factions, with only their wits and weapons to see them through the trials ahead.

subject: Air Temple power chamber
fact: The Air Temple’s power chamber is an octagonal room fifteen feet below the dungeon floor, lit by eerie milky radiance, with a polished gray stone floor shot through with mica, swirling glowing mist, a pierced bronze square, and a circular shaft over a pit. It is a sacred and hostile site of elemental power.
source_quote: The polished gray stone floor, shot through with glittering mica, was partially obscured by swirling, glowing mist. In the center stood a great pierced bronze square, and a circular shaft opened above a pit of the same diameter.

subject: Dick Rentsch’s deception
fact: It remains unclear whether Dick Rentsch’s failure to warn the party about the Air Temple’s territory was due to negligence, ignorance, or deliberate sabotage. His actions have placed them in extreme danger and may be part of a larger test or betrayal.
source_quote: Dick Rentsch had not simply sent them down a hallway—he had deposited them directly into enemy territory belonging to a rival elemental faction. Whether this was a test of their abilities or something more sinister remained unclear.

subject: the deeper secrets of the Temple
fact: Romag hinted that beyond the four elemental temples lie deeper levels containing unknown secrets and the true source of the Temple of Elemental Evil’s power. The party’s mission has only just begun.
source_quote: Below that lay the deeper temple and deeper secrets.

subject: session date
fact: The events described occurred during the party’s descent into the Temple of Elemental Evil, following their arrival at the Earth Temple and subsequent journey through the dungeon levels.
source_quote: The party descended once more, running quickly past the skeleton-filled corridor to avoid another encounter.
